claim: A relay cannot read a sealed note; only the addressed recipient opens it.
limitations: In-process and loopback only; not radio.
Relays still see packet sizes, timing and neighbors.

claim: Sealed notes are authenticated to the sender's key: a forged sender, a tampered ciphertext and an old-format packet fail to open.
limitations: Binds a public key, not a person.
A relay can still drop, delay or replay a genuine packet.
The construction has not been independently audited.

claim: The carrier relays only a finished raw transaction, never a PCZT.
limitations: Depends on a patched devtool.
Tested against a stub devtool; the real devtool path is shown by Runs A to C.

claim: The spend policy is checked before the wallet runs, and a denied payment runs the wallet zero times.
limitations: The policy bounds offline exposure; it does not prevent double-spend before broadcast.

claim: A gateway broadcasts a given transaction at most once; duplicates are dropped.
limitations: Shown on loopback with one gateway; multiple gateways were not run.

claim: Large transactions survive chunking, reordering and duplicate delivery.
limitations: Loopback only; no real lossy link was used.

claim: A shielded transaction can be built with every wallet step offline (Run A).
limitations: Run A was not broadcast.
Unified-address recipient: a 20,986-byte transaction.

claim: A transaction carried across the carrier unchanged was broadcast once and mined in testnet block 4,550,000 (Run B).
limitations: Loopback UDP on one machine.
Run B does not itself show an offline build; Runs A and C do.

claim: A ZIP 321 payment was built with every devtool step offline, handed over on loopback UDP, broadcast once and mined in testnet block 4,550,881 (Run C).
limitations: Loopback UDP on one machine; no radio.
The memo was not observed in either wallet's view.
Paid from a separate account holding an externally received note (ADR-0003).

claim: ZIP 321 payment requests encode and parse, and pay accepts a request URI.
limitations: A subset of ZIP 321: one payment, amount and memo.

claim: In a six-device simulation with four retransmit rounds, about 93% of runs deliver at 30% packet loss and about 72% at 40% (300 seeds per setting).
limitations: A re-implementation on the judge page, not the real carrier.
Not evidence about radio.
Single seeds in scripts/demo.js pass at 30% and fail at 40%.

claim: The judge page presents the story, the evidence and a labeled simulation, and builds to a static file.
limitations: Visuals were checked in a headless browser, not on a real device.
Hosting is delivery, not evidence.

claim: An offline-built transaction expires about 50 minutes after the wallet's last sync.
limitations: The tip the wallet believed at build time was not logged.
Whether a later expiry can be set offline is not verified.

claim: The devtool's PCZT path cannot sign a spend of an internal-scope change note (SaplingVerify(WrongFvkForNote)).
limitations: The cause was established from the devtool's source; a fix was not built or tested.

claim: The memo in a ZIP 321 request reaches the merchant.
limitations: Not observed in either wallet's view of Run C; the cause was not determined.
